rules.rule: Two beats; the second sentence lands the punch.
rules.canon_example: Die hond is onder die bed. Slim skuif, eerlikwaar.

rules.rule: Spoken Boland/Strand register: dis, daai, hey/nè, boet, jinne — never textbook.
rules.canon_example: Vat n sambreel net vir ingeval, ne.

rules.rule: Loans stay loans: braai, Weber, bakkie, aircon, vibes, show, mute, snooze, dashboard, playlist.
rules.canon_example: Die son is op airplane mode.

rules.rule: Localise the image, never translate the pun; find the Afrikaans joke.
rules.canon_example: Die son gaan af soos hy weet ons kyk.

rules.rule: Short words, short clauses; cut what English needed and Afrikaans doesn't.
rules.canon_example: Reën op 'n plaas is nie weer nie. Dis 'n salaris wat val.

rules.rule: The double negative closes naturally and never trips.
rules.canon_example: Die kole gaan nie hulself aansteek nie.

rules.rule: Nature is a person with attitude: the sun bunks, the sky sulks, the wind has opinions.
SA props and places carry the joke: Kaapse Dokter, tafeldoek, Sani Pass, Upington, Tupperware-deksel, Spur.
rules.canon_example: Die lug is die kleur van 'n ou Tupperware-deksel.

rules.rule: Dry understatement and the shrug beat exclamation.
rules.canon_example: Kon erger gewees het. Kon ook beter gewees het.

rules.rule: Times and numbers the SA way: 06:30, 9vm, 35 in die skadu.
rules.canon_example: 06:30 en die teer dink al aan smelt.
